actual_scope: One physical FANIN4 update in the aligned F2[C2^2] coefficient frame: four arbitrary read-only source vectors, one arbitrary dirty target, identity source maps, L=4 coefficients. Compare one synchronized in-place scan with four complete singleton scans, fully charging XORs, reads, writes, head travel, call records, source and target reference fields, scratch, and frame changes.
scope_change_reason: The original connector-alphabet card was refined after Cycle 43 PR #2249 established the exact abstract query/addition floor for arity-4..6 source calls at full per-tap cost. This task changes the operation granularity to one explicit aligned physical stream macro and checks its complete lower-level traffic bill. It preserves the four source XORs per coefficient and makes no full-batch or exponent claim.
bottleneck_link: Recursive source calls also require data movement and complete head restoration. A fused source update can reduce that implementation bill while keeping the abstract source-add count unchanged. The benefit reaches the selected construction only if emitted source roles are already aligned in a live supplier frame.
stop_rule: Stop after one FANIN4 map in F2[C2^2], its exact general-L identity and cost formula, and exhaustive verification of all 2^20 dirty states at L=4. Do not expand to the 63-mask batch or claim supplier admission.
evidence: The fused scan has reads=20, writes=4, XORs=16, head_moves=40, call_records=1, source_refs=4, target_refs=1 at L=4. Four singleton updates have reads=32, writes=16, XORs=16, head_moves=64, call_records=4, source_refs=4, target_refs=4. Both restore all heads and preserve all sources. At uniform per-record price d the weighted saving is (s-1)(L*r+L*w+2L*h+d+t); for variable record prices d1 and ds it is (s-1)L(r+w+2h)+s*d1-ds+(s-1)t, less any opcode-table or frame-conversion expense F. Equal unit prices on all listed resources give an exact net saving of 54 units. The verifier checks all 1,048,576 arbitrary dirty L=4 states and five failure controls. No supplier mapping or kappa change.
author: Cinna Davis
